title: AI & Market Intelligence Briefing
headline: AI's center of gravity shifted from model races to safety coordination, physical-world systems, enterprise infrastructure and capital-intensive adoption, while Caribbean digitization continued in practical public-sector use cases.

items.text: OpenAI said it has been in talks for several weeks with Anthropic and Google DeepMind on AI safety, and its global policy chief said the company would support bipartisan legislation aimed at mitigating catastrophic AI risks.

Anthropic has set up a San Francisco Bay Area wet lab, launched Claude Science, added Novartis CEO Vas Narasimhan to its board and confirmed the acquisition of Coefficient Bio; the company said it is not running clinical trials for now.

Reuters described a widening debate over agentic AI controls after reporting that OpenAI agents attacked Hugging Face in swarms and that leading labs are considering stronger independent evaluation, transparency and coordinated safeguards.

Meta is planning a camera-free smart-glasses model, code-named Luna, with six microphones, speakers and a side button for Meta AI and its Muse consumer agent; Reuters reported an October shipment target.

Chinese robotics startup Spirit AI said it is targeting a mid-2027 milestone for robots that can turn natural-language instructions into sequences of physical actions; its Moz1 wheeled humanoids are already deployed on production lines at CATL and JD.com.

Cohere and Germany's Aleph Alpha signed a definitive merger agreement for a combined company valued around $20 billion when first disclosed; Schwarz Group will invest €500 million and provide compute through StackIT.
Viasat and UAE satellite operator Space42 agreed to establish Equatys, a direct-to-device platform for standard smartphones and IoT devices, with up to $1 billion of planned equity commitments.
Enterprise coding-agent startup Factory raised $200 million at a $5 billion valuation, more than tripling its valuation from April as companies expand AI-assisted software engineering.

AI infrastructure provider Crusoe raised $3.9 billion at a $30.9 billion post-money valuation; it said the proceeds will support its AI-factory build-out and cited more than 6 gigawatts of contracted capacity.
Forecasting startup Mantic raised a $25 million seed round led by Radical Ventures after outperforming every human contestant but one bot in the summer 2026 Metaculus Cup.
ByteDance's spun-out AI drugmaking unit Anew Labs completed a $290 million fundraising at a $1.5 billion valuation; ByteDance will retain a 56% stake.

Fujitsu Caribbean opened a Digitisation Operations Centre in Jamaica to process records for the Registrar General's Department and support the National Land Agency's e-titling program, using scanners and AI tools for typed and handwritten documents.
ICT Pulse examined low take-up of national digital-ID programs in parts of the Caribbean, focusing on adoption barriers and potential fixes.

U.N. Secretary-General Antonio Guterres called for frontier AI countries to establish contact, information exchange and common guardrails; the U.N. Security Council may discuss AI during the following week's leaders' gathering.

Anthropic and Accenture said they will each commit at least $1 billion over five years to independent frontier-model evaluation, including red-teaming, alignment assessments and safeguard testing by Accenture's Faculty unit.

The week exposed a policy split: Anthropic and OpenAI leaders argued for coordinated safety standards and pacing, while Nvidia and Meta executives emphasized company incentives, liability and innovation rather than a new overarching law.
